Under Emperor Claudius, 30,000 workers spent eleven years carving a nearly 3.7-mile (6-kilometer) passage through a mountain to manage the waters of Lake Fucino. description: Your morning coffee may do more than wake you up. Scientists have uncovered a surprising connection between caffeine, cellular repair, and aging.

description: Scientists have identified a previously unknown drainage pathway at the back of the eye that carries fluid into the body's lymphatic system. title: Archaeologists Opened Six Ancient Pits in China and Found 17,000 Relics From a Lost Era
description: A city lost its status, another rose to prominence. Now, extraordinary objects buried 3,000 years ago are helping reveal when it happened.

title: A 345-Million-Year-Old Fossil Has Turned a Decades-Old Scientific Theory on Its Head
description: A 345-million-year-old fossil discovered in Scotland has been reclassified after advanced X-ray imaging revealed anatomical features that had remained hidden for decades. Once regarded as one of the earliest reptile relatives adapted to life on land, the animal possessed internal gills and a fish-like mouth, suggesting a much closer relationship to ancient aquatic vertebrates.

title: Some Dying Patients Have One Last Clear Conversation With Their Families, and Science Still Can’t Explain Why

description: Researchers in Germany have identified a bacterial enzyme capable of breaking down certain biodegradable plastics and penicillin antibiotics. The finding reveals an unexpected connection between plastic degradation and a biological process associated with antibiotic resistance.

title: The Chestnut Tree Was Once Everywhere in America. Then It Almost Disappeared
description: The American chestnut once covered vast stretches of the eastern United States, providing food, timber, and shelter across an extensive forest ecosystem. By the middle of the 20th century, a fungal disease introduced from Asia had destroyed nearly four billion trees, transforming forests that had supported wildlife and communities for generations.

title: Divers Found the World’s First Computer in a Greek Shipwreck, but Most of It Is Still Missing
description: Ancient bronze gears, buried in a Greek shipwreck for 2,000 years, continue to puzzle researchers studying a remarkable device designed to track the stars.

title: This 300-Year-Old Machine Predicted One of the Biggest Problems With Modern AI
description: Jonathan Swift’s 1726 novel Gulliver’s Travels contains a fictional machine designed to produce written knowledge without requiring its users to study. Nearly 300 years later, the invention has drawn comparisons with artificial intelligence chatbots and the questions surrounding their ability to generate reliable information.

title: The Soviet Union Lost Contact With a 19-Ton Space Station in 1985, Then Sent Two Cosmonauts to Save It and They Found Its Interior Frozen
description: With frozen water tanks and dead batteries aboard Salyut 7, two cosmonauts faced a difficult rescue mission that demanded precise flying and complex repairs.

title: Archaeologists Uncovered Ancient Wood Tools in Spain, Including a Mysterious Neanderthal Club
description: Archaeologists have identified 13 wooden artifacts associated with Neanderthals at a prehistoric rock shelter in Spain. The discoveries include hunting spears, possible bark containers and an unusually shaped club with no known equivalent in the prehistoric record.

description: A 93-country study links cat density, happiness and Toxoplasma exposure, revealing an unexpected pattern researchers say needs closer study.

title: A Russian Lab Worker Died After a Possible Plague Exposure at a High-Security Research Facility in Siberia
description: A 28-year-old laboratory worker in Russia died from pneumonia on October 2 after reportedly being exposed to Yersinia pestis, the bacterium that causes plague, at a specialized biodefense research institute in Irkutsk.

title: Something Troubling Is Happening to Switzerland’s Glaciers, New Data Reveals
description: Switzerland’s glaciers lost 5.5% of their remaining ice volume during the 2025–2026 hydrological year, marking the country’s second-worst annual glacier loss on record. The latest measurements also show that nearly 20% of Swiss glacier ice has disappeared since 2021, following five consecutive years of unusually rapid melting.

title: The Medieval World Had Its Own ‘Deepfake’ Document, and Church Officials Used It for Centuries to Expand Their Power
description: One forged document claimed to hand Rome and the West to the pope. Its influence lasted centuries before scholars proved it was fake.

title: Giant Fossil Turtle Found in the Amazon Reveals a Lost World of Massive Reptiles
description: Two fossil turtle shells recovered from the Peruvian Amazon have provided new evidence of the enormous size reached by Chelus colombiana, an extinct freshwater species that inhabited northern South America during the Miocene. The larger specimen measures 84.6 centimeters (2.8 feet) in shell length and belonged to an animal estimated to weigh approximately 65 kilograms (143 pounds).

title: Paris Wasn’t Always Paris. Archaeologists May Have Just Found the Lost City That Came Before It
description: Fire traces, Gallic construction methods and period artifacts found beneath Hôtel-Dieu are reopening the debate over the birthplace of ancient Paris.

description: Crews clearing debris below Hagia Sophia revealed miles of forgotten tunnels, hidden chambers and an enigmatic passage with no clear purpose.

title: Scientists Can Now Rebuild Images From Brain Scans, and Dreams Could Be Next
description: Brain scans are becoming readable in a new way. AI can now reconstruct viewed images with far more detail than earlier systems achieved.

title: These Brain Neurons May Reveal a New Way to Tackle Hard-to-Control Hypertension
description: Scientists have identified a brain circuit that may contribute to neurogenic hypertension by linking breathing-related activity with the sympathetic nervous system. In experiments on rats, suppressing neurons in a region called the lateral parafacial area, or pFL, eliminated abnormal sympathetic activity associated with expiration and returned arterial pressure to normal levels.

title: North Korea Set Off Its Biggest Nuclear Test Beneath This Mountain, and the Ground Is Still Shaking Years Later
description: The blast ended in 2017, but the ground did not settle. Researchers now link years of seismic activity to reawakened faults beneath Mt. Mantap.

title: A Quick Stop in Norway Revealed Carvings That Had Survived for 3,000 Years
description: A drive through Bærum in eastern Norway led to the discovery of a group of rock carvings believed to date back roughly 3,000 years. Experienced rock-art hunter Tormod Fjeld and his daughter Ada stopped beneath Kolsåstoppen after the landscape caught Fjeld’s attention, revealing ships, a large footprint and a hand carved into exposed sandstone.

title: What Is Leaking From Arctic Permafrost Could Quietly Make Global Warming Worse
description: Across the Arctic, ground that remained frozen for centuries or millennia is thawing, allowing long-stored organic material to decompose and release carbon dioxide and methane. The process is changing permafrost from a reservoir of carbon into a source of greenhouse gases, while also weakening the ground beneath roads, buildings and other infrastructure.

title: They Walked Past This Old Church Chest for Years, Now Experts Think It Could Be Centuries Old
description: Hidden for years in a village presbytery, an unusual wooden chest is now raising questions about its age, purpose and possible historic value.

title: This Record-Breaking Star System Is Putting Einstein’s Theory to a Remarkable Test

title: Napoleon’s Mysterious 1809 Letter Has Been Decoded After More Than Two Centuries

title: Perseverance Finds Evidence That Water Changed Mars Again and Again

Instead of finding mainly sedimentary rocks along the crater’s ancient shoreline, the rover encountered igneous rocks that preserve evidence of groundwater, lake-related alteration and later hydrothermal activity.

description: Strange oxygen readings from the Pacific abyss are pushing researchers to investigate whether metal-rich nodules can drive unseen chemical reactions.

title: Germany Just Built the World’s Tallest Turbine, Towering Above the Eiffel Tower
description: Germany has completed the main structure of what its developer describes as the world’s tallest wind turbine, a 365-meter, or 1,197-foot, installation in Schipkau in eastern Germany. The experimental turbine will test whether stronger and steadier winds at 300 meters can significantly increase electricity generation without requiring a larger rotor.

The material, ytterbium diantimonide, or YbSb2, develops tiny internal magnetic fields when it enters its superconducting state.

title: Flies Exposed to Almost No Magnetic Field Revealed a Strange Aging Effect
description: Reducing Earth’s magnetic field to near-zero levels changed lifespan, movement and mitochondrial activity in fruit flies, with the effects differing sharply between healthy animals and flies carrying a genetic defect linked to mitochondrial dysfunction. The findings come from experiments led by researchers at the University of Nottingham and published in the journal Aging in September 2026.

title: Astronomers Capture a Young Planet Stirring Its Birthplace for the First Time
description: Astronomers have directly imaged gas interacting with a forming planet in the WISPIT 2 system, giving researchers a detailed view of how a young giant planet influences the material from which it is still growing. title: Current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August: RBI data
description: India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data released by the RBI on Thursday. The net deficit in the merchandise trade account declined to USD 26.6 billion in August from USD 27.6 billion in the same month last year. Merchandise exports rose to USD 44.7 billion in August from USD 35.1 billion a year ago, while imports increased to USD 71.3 billion from USD 62.7 billion, the RBI data showed. The surplus in services trade increased to USD 16.5 billion in August from USD 15.6 billion a year ago. Services exports rose to USD 35.5 billion from USD 31.2 billion, while imports increased to USD 18.9 billion from USD 15.6 billion. Net transfers, including remittances, increased to USD 12.8 billion in August from USD 12.2 billion a year ago, while the net deficit in the income account widened to USD 8 billion from USD 6.3 .
